strings.name: Daddy Yankee
strings.summary: Born Ramón Luis Ayala Rodríguez, Daddy Yankee developed in Puerto Rico’s underground scene into a leading reggaeton artist. Gasolina and Despacito with Luis Fonsi expanded the genre’s global audience. After announcing a farewell tour in 2022 and publicly embracing Christianity in 2023, he resumed recording. He released La Postal in 2026 and received the Latin Recording Academy’s Person of the Year honor.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Through works such as Gasolina, he helped reggaeton enter the global pop market and spread Puerto Rican urban music culture.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: San Juan, Puerto Rico; sources give 1976 or 1977 as his birth year, both on February 3.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and beginnings
strings.facts.f2.value: Joined underground recording projects including DJ Playero’s as a teenager; earlier hoped to play professional baseball.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Spreading reggaeton globally
strings.highlights.h1.text: Gasolina and collaborations helped Puerto Rican urban music reach international pop audiences.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Continued work and industry recognition
strings.highlights.h2.text: Returned to recording after farewell touring and received the 2026 Latin Recording Academy Person of the Year honor.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Honored as Person of the Year
strings.timeline.t1.text: The Latin Recording Academy celebrated his career at its formal Las Vegas gala.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Released La Postal
strings.timeline.t2.text: A new concept album used reggaeton to tell emotional and personal stories.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Released Christian-themed album
strings.timeline.t3.text: Lamento en Baile became a major recording after his public turn toward faith.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Ended farewell shows and declared faith
strings.timeline.t4.text: Publicly embraced Christianity at the Puerto Rico tour finale, later continuing to record.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Released Legendaddy
strings.timeline.t5.text: Released an album and announced farewell touring, temporarily ending large-scale tours.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Collaborated on Despacito
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined Luis Fonsi on the song, with the original and later remix achieving global success.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Broke through with Barrio Fino and Gasolina
strings.timeline.t7.text: Album and single helped reggaeton reach a much wider international pop market.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Released solo debut
strings.timeline.t8.text: Independently released No Mercy, developing his early solo recording style.
strings.timeline.t9.title: Joined Playero underground recordings
strings.timeline.t9.text: Appeared in DJ Playero’s projects, entering Puerto Rico’s urban music scene.
